$comment: POSIX `environ` — the SMOKE TEST that reading the environment through the `environ` DSS's <unistd.h> declares on elf (the shipped data-object row) WORKS in a DSS-built ELF exec on both arches, debug and release. ★★ READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING WHAT IT PROVES, BECAUSE IT ONCE PROVED LESS THAN IT CLAIMED: this program is a SELF-LOOP and CANNOT witness an OBJECT-IDENTITY property. It read `environ` through the DSS macro and cross-checked against libc's own `getenv`, but under the ELF COPY RELOCATION binding that shipped at the time BOTH reads went through the very name the exec CLAIMED, so it compared the exec's copy WITH ITSELF — structurally unable to fail. It stayed GREEN on all four legs across the entire window in which a third-party libtcl8.6.so reading the UN-PREFIXED `environ` got NULL and SIGSEGV'd in TclSetupEnv+0xe8 (regression pair `09e1608a` green -> `6f4aab73` rc=139, introduced by `64ee3a16`). ★★★ THE GENERAL RULE that came out of it: AN OBJECT-IDENTITY PROPERTY CANNOT BE WITNESSED BY ONE IMAGE — a test asserting that a symbol denotes the SAME OBJECT must involve a SECOND image DSS did not build. That witness is examples/c/environ_alias_object_identity, which dlopens a gcc-built `.so` reading the un-prefixed name, asserts the VALUE it sees (never mere survival), asserts dlsym SAME_OBJECT=YES on both spellings, and verifies the shipped `.so` itself really relocates against `environ` before trusting it. ⇒ THIS example is kept for what it DOES witness — a live, well-formed environment vector reachable through the shipped descriptor on both ELF arches, debug and release — and NOT for object identity (D-LK-ELF-COPY-RELOC-CLAIMS-ONE-NAME-OF-AN-ALIAS-SET). BINDING MODEL: every ELF format declares dataImportBinding:got-indirect — the exec reserves a GOT slot per imported object, emits one R_*_GLOB_DAT against it, ld.so writes the LIBRARY object's ADDRESS into the slot at load, and the shared GotIndirect lowering (lea-of-slot + deref) reads it; the exec DEFINES NOTHING (its data-import dynsym rows stay UNDEF, st_size 0). The copy-relocation alternative is DELETED from the vocabulary. WHY `environ` RATHER THAN main's third parameter: POSIX.1 does not specify that parameter at all, so `extern char **environ;` (glibc /usr/include/unistd.h) is the interface portable code actually uses. WHICH SYMBOL (P68 round 11, D-FFI-ENVIRON-NOT-SHIPPED): `environ` itself — a data-object row on elf and macho, which glibc exports (WEAK) at the one address it also exports as `_environ` and `__environ`. It used to be an elf macro onto the STRONG `__environ`, a copy-relocation-era choice (the claimed name decided which object the exec read); under got-indirect every spelling resolves to glibc's ONE object, and the macro could not serve a program's own `extern char **environ;` in a TU without <unistd.h> — the POSIX spelling, witnessed on every pair by examples/c/environ_declared_by_the_program. EAGER-IMPORT SAFE, MEASURED before the row shipped on both run legs and two concurring instruments: glibc exports all three spellings at ONE address — `__environ` STRONG (`B`/`g`), `environ`/`_environ` WEAK (`V`/`w`) — 0x20ad58 @GLIBC_2.2.5 (x86_64) and 0x1b7288 @GLIBC_2.17 (aarch64), `nm -D` and `objdump -T` concurring with `DO .bss` SIZE 8. ⚠ the `@@GLIBC_x.y` suffix makes a grep anchored on `$` report a FALSE ABSENT. THE ENVIRONMENT'S CONTENT IS NEVER ASSERTED (it is host-dependent) — only its STRUCTURE plus an agreement check, so the stdout pin is host-independent: every entry must be NAME=VALUE with a non-empty NAME (exit 2/3 — a binding one indirection off, the got-indirect-WITHOUT-deref class, fails the '=' scan on garbage rather than appearing to pass), the vector must be non-empty (exit 4), and environ[0]'s NAME is looked up through libc's OWN getenv with the value required BYTE-IDENTICAL to the text after '=' (exit 7 = getenv cannot see a variable environ claims exists; exit 8 = they disagree). ⚠ THAT AGREEMENT CHECK IS THE SELF-LOOP HALF: getenv reads libc's internal `__environ`, the same object this program reads, so it detects a garbage or stale pointer but NEVER a split. ELF-ONLY on purpose: this program reads `environ` as <unistd.h> declares it, and only glibc's <unistd.h> does that (under _GNU_SOURCE) — Apple's never declares it, and pe's `environ` is <stdlib.h>'s macro onto the UCRT accessor (✔MEASURED, NEITHER Windows CRT exports a data `environ`: ucrtbase.dll (2,484 exports) has no `environ`/`_environ`/`__environ`, msvcrt.dll (1,330) only the UNDERSCORED `_environ`, ordinal 270) — so a Mach-O or pe arm of THIS program would have no reference behind it. The spelling every platform shares, the program's own declaration, is witnessed on all five pairs by examples/c/environ_declared_by_the_program. exec-only, not pie: the canonical elf data-object witness (stdio_stream_objects) is likewise exec-only, and this defect was the EXEC arm's. RED-ON-DISABLE: un-ship the `environ` row -> S_UndeclaredIdentifier `environ` at compile time (MEASURED 2026-09-24, both arches, debug and release); drop dataImportBinding from the elf exec format -> K_FormatLacksImportSupport at link; neuter the got-indirect deref (a bare lea) -> the vector walk reads the slot's own address as environ[0] and fails the '=' scan at exit 2. ⓘ The row's SPELLING is not red-on-disable here, and that is exactly why the sibling example exists: `environ` and `__environ` resolve to one object under got-indirect, where under copy relocation the weak spelling returned 1 with no diagnostic. Cross-checked in WSL against `gcc -std=gnu17 -D_GNU_SOURCE -no-pie` (exit 42, identical stdout; MEASURED 2026-09-24) — `-D_GNU_SOURCE` because glibc declares `environ` only under __USE_GNU, which no -std mode defines for C: plain `-std=gnu17 -no-pie` refuses it ('environ' undeclared).
